verses.1: For the choirmaster. A psalm of David.
verses.2: Listen, God, to my voice in my plea to you, from fear of an enemy rescue my life.
verses.3: Conceal me from the hidden counsel of the evildoers, from the riot of the workers of iniquity.
verses.4: Those who sharpen their tongues like a sword, who aim their arrows, a bitter word.
verses.5: Lest they aim at the blameless in secret, suddenly they shoot at them, and do not fear.
verses.6: They strengthen for themselves a harmful word; they recount plans for a snare. They say, "Who will see it?"
verses.7: They search for iniquity, they diligently seek it out. The inward man and the deep heart.
verses.8: But God shot an arrow, suddenly their wounds were struck.
verses.9: Their own tongues overwhelmed them. All who see them are appalled.
verses.10: All mankind feared, and declared the works of God, and understood his deeds.
verses.11: The righteous will rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in him. All the upright in heart will exult.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "For the choirmaster" is a standard musical instruction in the psalms, rendered from "לַמְנַצֵּחַ" as in many modern translations.
- v. 5: "Suddenly they shoot at them" reflects "פִתְאֹם יֹרֻהוּ" and is used in place of "suddenly they shoot it" to keep the focus on the blameless being targeted.
- v. 7: The phrase "the inward man and the deep heart" is an interpretive rendering of "וְקֶרֶב אִישׁ וְלֵב עָמֹק," which combines a human and an inner depth, likely referring to the hidden motives of the evildoers.
